metadata.title: Longo.org Cyber History Calendar
metadata.description: Canonical source dataset for the Longo.org Cyber History Calendar.

event.title: Fred Cohen virus demonstration
event.summary: Fred Cohen demonstrated self-replicating code during academic security research, helping formalize the modern computer-virus concept.
event.whyItStillMatters: It helped turn malicious self-replication into a defined computer-security problem.

event.title: Brain boot-sector virus
event.summary: Brain spread through infected floppy-disk boot sectors and is widely cited as the first IBM PC-compatible virus to circulate broadly.
event.whyItStillMatters: It marks malware's transition from research curiosity to something that could spread through ordinary computer use.

event.title: Morris Worm
event.summary: The Morris Worm spread rapidly across the early Internet, exploiting multiple weaknesses and affecting thousands of systems.
event.whyItStillMatters: It became a foundational Internet security incident and helped drive organized incident-response capability.

event.title: CERT Coordination Center established
event.summary: DARPA funded creation of the CERT Coordination Center at Carnegie Mellon after the Morris Worm.
event.whyItStillMatters: Modern incident coordination and vulnerability-response practices trace directly to needs exposed by early Internet-wide incidents.

event.title: AIDS Trojan / PC Cyborg
event.summary: The AIDS Trojan was distributed on floppy disks, hid directories, encrypted filenames, and demanded payment by postal mail.
event.whyItStillMatters: Often cited as the first ransomware, it proves the extortion model predates cryptocurrency by decades.

event.title: UK Computer Misuse Act
event.summary: The United Kingdom enacted the Computer Misuse Act, creating criminal offenses for unauthorized access and related computer misuse.
event.whyItStillMatters: It became a foundational cybercrime statute and still shapes debates over authorization and security research.

event.title: First DEF CON
event.summary: The first DEF CON brought hackers, researchers, and security practitioners together in Las Vegas.
event.whyItStillMatters: DEF CON became one of the most influential forums for practical security research and hacker culture.

event.title: SSL 2.0 era begins
event.summary: Netscape introduced SSL to protect web communications and support secure commercial use of the Internet.
event.whyItStillMatters: Encrypted web transport became a basic expectation for online trust, despite weaknesses in early versions.

event.title: Back Orifice released
event.summary: Cult of the Dead Cow released Back Orifice, a remote-administration tool that could covertly control Windows systems.
event.whyItStillMatters: It popularized the concept of remote-access trojans and abuse of legitimate administration functions.

event.title: Melissa
event.summary: Melissa spread through infected Word documents and Outlook address books, disrupting enterprise mail systems.
event.whyItStillMatters: Attackers still win by abusing trust, familiar file formats, and legitimate communication channels.

event.title: CIH / Chernobyl virus
event.summary: CIH overwrote hard-drive data and, on some systems, flash BIOS content when it activated.
event.whyItStillMatters: It is an early example of malware designed for destructive impact beyond nuisance or propagation.

event.title: CVE initiative launched
event.summary: MITRE launched Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures to give publicly known vulnerabilities standardized identifiers.
event.whyItStillMatters: CVE created a shared language for vulnerability management across vendors, scanners, advisories, and defenders.

event.title: Major Internet DDoS attacks
event.summary: Distributed denial-of-service attacks disrupted major Internet properties including Yahoo, Amazon, CNN, and eBay.
event.whyItStillMatters: They demonstrated that even major online services could be overwhelmed through coordinated abuse of compromised systems.

event.title: ILOVEYOU / Love Letter worm
event.summary: The Love Letter worm spread through a malicious Visual Basic Script attachment and automated forwarding.
event.whyItStillMatters: It combined human psychology with automated propagation, a pattern still visible in modern phishing and malware delivery.

event.title: Anna Kournikova worm
event.summary: A social-engineering worm disguised as an image of tennis player Anna Kournikova spread widely through email.
event.whyItStillMatters: Compelling lures and trusted communication channels remain durable malware-delivery techniques.

event.title: Code Red
event.summary: Code Red exploited a vulnerability in Microsoft IIS and infected hundreds of thousands of Internet-facing systems.
event.whyItStillMatters: Self-propagating attacks against exposed infrastructure can move faster than human remediation processes.

event.title: Nimda
event.summary: Nimda spread through email, network shares, compromised websites, vulnerable IIS servers, and earlier backdoors.
event.whyItStillMatters: It demonstrated the danger of combining multiple propagation vectors into one campaign.

event.title: Klez worm surge
event.summary: Klez became a widespread email worm, spoofing sender addresses and distributing infected attachments.
event.whyItStillMatters: Sender spoofing and trusted-channel abuse remain basic ingredients of modern social engineering.

event.title: SQL Slammer
event.summary: Slammer exploited a previously patched SQL Server flaw and caused a dramatic global traffic spike.
event.whyItStillMatters: It remains a classic example of how quickly a worm can weaponize a known vulnerability when patching lags.

event.title: Blaster worm
event.summary: Blaster exploited a previously patched Windows RPC vulnerability and scanned continuously for additional vulnerable hosts.
event.whyItStillMatters: It illustrates the persistent gap between patch availability and actual remediation.

event.title: Sobig.F
event.summary: Sobig.F spread through email at enormous scale and generated significant mail disruption.
event.whyItStillMatters: Mass-mailing malware showed how compromised endpoints could become infrastructure for large-scale abuse.

event.title: Mydoom
event.summary: Mydoom spread through email and peer-to-peer networks, opened a backdoor, and launched denial-of-service activity.
event.whyItStillMatters: Compromised endpoints quickly became infrastructure for further attacks, a pattern still seen in botnets.

event.title: Sasser
event.summary: Sasser exploited the Windows LSASS vulnerability and could propagate without a user opening an attachment.
event.whyItStillMatters: It reinforced the risk of rapid exploitation following vulnerability disclosure.

event.title: PCI DSS 1.0
event.summary: Major payment-card brands created the first Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard.
event.whyItStillMatters: PCI DSS became one of the most influential industry security compliance baselines.

event.title: Zotob worm
event.summary: Zotob exploited a recently disclosed Windows Plug and Play vulnerability and disrupted corporate and media networks.
event.whyItStillMatters: It showed how quickly exploit code can follow a patch and why emergency vulnerability management matters.

event.title: WMF vulnerability crisis
event.summary: A Windows Metafile vulnerability enabled drive-by exploitation through malicious images and triggered an out-of-cycle security update.
event.whyItStillMatters: Content-parsing flaws can create code-execution paths through routine web browsing.

event.title: TJX breach disclosed
event.summary: TJX disclosed unauthorized access affecting payment-card and customer data across its retail operations.
event.whyItStillMatters: The breach became an early large-scale example of wireless security, card-data, and third-party risk failures.

event.title: Estonia cyberattacks begin
event.summary: Estonian government, banking, media, and other online services experienced sustained disruptive cyber activity amid political tensions.
event.whyItStillMatters: The attacks became a landmark case in national cyber defense, resilience, and geopolitical cyber disruption.

event.title: Kaminsky DNS flaw disclosed
event.summary: Dan Kaminsky disclosed a fundamental DNS cache-poisoning weakness after a coordinated multi-vendor patch effort.
event.whyItStillMatters: The episode showed the systemic risk of flaws in core Internet infrastructure and the value of coordinated disclosure.

event.title: MS08-067 emergency patch
event.summary: Microsoft issued an out-of-band critical update for a remotely exploitable Windows Server service vulnerability.
event.whyItStillMatters: The flaw was later exploited by Conficker and remains a classic emergency-patching case.

event.title: Conficker discovered
event.summary: Conficker exploited the Windows Server service vulnerability addressed by MS08-067 and added multiple propagation techniques.
event.whyItStillMatters: It showed how unpatched systems, weak credentials, removable media, and shares can combine into durable malware spread.

event.title: Heartland Payment Systems breach discovered
event.summary: Heartland discovered a major payment-card breach involving malware in transaction-processing systems.
event.whyItStillMatters: The case became an important milestone in payment-security accountability and processor risk.

event.title: U.S. and South Korea DDoS attacks
event.summary: Government, financial, and media websites in the United States and South Korea were targeted by coordinated denial-of-service attacks.
event.whyItStillMatters: The campaign reinforced the use of botnets for politically significant disruption and the difficulty of attribution.

event.title: Operation Aurora disclosed
event.summary: Google disclosed a sophisticated targeted intrusion that stole intellectual property and affected numerous large companies.
event.whyItStillMatters: Aurora was a watershed moment in public corporate disclosure of nation-state activity.

event.title: Stuxnet first identified
event.summary: Security researchers identified malware later shown to target specific industrial-control environments.
event.whyItStillMatters: Its discovery marked a turning point in awareness of cyber weapons designed to manipulate physical processes.

event.title: ICS-CERT Stuxnet advisory
event.summary: ICS-CERT documented Stuxnet targeting Siemens industrial-control software and using multiple advanced propagation techniques.
event.whyItStillMatters: Stuxnet permanently changed the conversation around cyber-physical risk.

event.title: RSA SecurID breach disclosed
event.summary: RSA disclosed an advanced persistent threat and warned that information related to SecurID products had been extracted.
event.whyItStillMatters: Security controls with privileged trust relationships are strategic targets in their own right.

event.title: Comodo certificate compromise
event.summary: A certificate-authority reseller account was compromised and used to issue fraudulent certificates for major online services.
event.whyItStillMatters: Web trust depends on the operational security of certificate-issuance infrastructure, not cryptography alone.

event.title: PlayStation Network breach disclosed
event.summary: Sony disclosed a major compromise of PlayStation Network and Qriocity user data after taking services offline.
event.whyItStillMatters: The incident highlighted large-scale consumer identity exposure and the operational cost of prolonged outages.

event.title: DigiNotar fraudulent certificates exposed
event.summary: Fraudulent certificates issued after compromise of DigiNotar were discovered, ultimately destroying trust in the certificate authority.
event.whyItStillMatters: Compromise of one PKI trust anchor can create ecosystem-wide consequences.

event.title: Flame malware revealed
event.summary: Researchers disclosed Flame, a sophisticated espionage platform used primarily in the Middle East.
event.whyItStillMatters: Flame illustrated the growing complexity and modularity of state-aligned cyber espionage tooling.

event.title: LinkedIn password breach
event.summary: Millions of hashed LinkedIn passwords were posted online following a breach.
event.whyItStillMatters: The incident reinforced the importance of strong password hashing, unique credentials, and resistance to credential reuse.

event.title: Shamoon attacks Saudi Aramco
event.summary: Shamoon was used in a destructive attack that wiped large numbers of Saudi Aramco workstations.
event.whyItStillMatters: The attack demonstrated the business impact of destructive malware and the importance of segmentation and recovery.

event.title: Mandiant APT1 report
event.summary: Mandiant published a detailed report linking a large cyber-espionage campaign to a unit of China's People's Liberation Army.
event.whyItStillMatters: The report helped normalize evidence-based public attribution of state-sponsored cyber operations.

event.title: DarkSeoul attacks
event.summary: Cyberattacks disrupted major South Korean banks and broadcasters, wiping systems and affecting operations.
event.whyItStillMatters: The incident showed how destructive malware can be used for national-level disruption.

event.title: Adobe breach disclosed
event.summary: Adobe disclosed an intrusion involving customer information and source code.
event.whyItStillMatters: The breach illustrated the value attackers place on both identity data and proprietary software source code.

event.title: Target breach announced
event.summary: Target confirmed unauthorized access to payment-card data affecting tens of millions of accounts.
event.whyItStillMatters: The breach became a landmark example of third-party access risk, point-of-sale compromise, and executive accountability.

event.title: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 1.0
event.summary: NIST released the first Framework for Improving Critical Infrastructure Cybersecurity.
event.whyItStillMatters: The Framework created a common risk-based language for cybersecurity outcomes and executive communication.

event.title: Heartbleed
event.summary: Heartbleed exposed a flaw in OpenSSL heartbeat handling that allowed remote attackers to read portions of process memory.
event.whyItStillMatters: It showed how one defect in a ubiquitous security library can create global risk and require key rotation beyond patching.

event.title: Home Depot breach disclosed
event.summary: Home Depot disclosed a payment-card breach involving malware on point-of-sale systems.
event.whyItStillMatters: Retail breaches reinforced the need for segmentation, payment-environment hardening, and third-party access controls.

event.title: Shellshock
event.summary: Shellshock allowed arbitrary command execution through crafted environment variables processed by GNU Bash.
event.whyItStillMatters: It demonstrated the systemic risk created when foundational components are embedded across enormous software estates.

event.title: JPMorgan Chase breach disclosed
event.summary: JPMorgan Chase disclosed a major intrusion affecting contact information associated with tens of millions of households and small businesses.
event.whyItStillMatters: The incident underscored the scale and attractiveness of identity data held by financial institutions.

event.title: POODLE disclosed
event.summary: Researchers disclosed a weakness in SSL 3.0 that could allow recovery of plaintext from encrypted connections.
event.whyItStillMatters: Legacy compatibility can preserve attack paths long after stronger replacements exist.

event.title: Sony Pictures destructive attack
event.summary: Sony Pictures suffered a destructive intrusion involving malware, stolen data, and major operational disruption.
event.whyItStillMatters: The attack showed how theft, coercion, public disclosure, and destruction can be combined in one campaign.

event.title: Anthem breach disclosed
event.summary: Anthem disclosed unauthorized access to a database containing information on current and former members and employees.
event.whyItStillMatters: Healthcare identity data has long-lived value and creates exposure that persists well beyond incident containment.

event.title: OPM breach announced
event.summary: The U.S. Office of Personnel Management disclosed a major incident affecting federal personnel and background-investigation data.
event.whyItStillMatters: The breach demonstrated the intelligence value of aggregated identity and personnel information.

event.title: Hacking Team breach
event.summary: Hacking Team's internal data and source code were leaked following a compromise.
event.whyItStillMatters: The breach exposed the commercial offensive-security ecosystem and fueled debate over zero-day markets and surveillance technology.

event.title: Ashley Madison breach disclosed
event.summary: Attackers disclosed a compromise of Ashley Madison and later released stolen user data.
event.whyItStillMatters: The incident highlighted the personal, legal, and reputational consequences of breaches involving highly sensitive behavioral data.

event.title: Ukraine power grid cyberattack
event.summary: A coordinated cyber operation disrupted electricity distribution in Ukraine through enterprise compromise and control-system access.
event.whyItStillMatters: It became one of the defining examples of cyber operations causing real-world critical-infrastructure disruption.

event.title: Bangladesh Bank cyber heist
event.summary: Attackers used compromised systems and fraudulent SWIFT messages in an attempt to steal nearly $1 billion from Bangladesh Bank.
event.whyItStillMatters: The heist showed how cyber compromise can manipulate trusted financial messaging and payment processes.

event.title: Hollywood Presbyterian ransomware payment
event.summary: A hospital paid ransom after ransomware disrupted access to systems and records.
event.whyItStillMatters: Healthcare became one of the earliest sectors to show how ransomware could affect service delivery and patient-care operations.

event.title: DNC intrusion disclosed
event.summary: The Democratic National Committee disclosed a network compromise attributed by investigators to Russian intelligence-linked groups.
event.whyItStillMatters: The incident became a landmark example of cyber-enabled information operations intersecting with political processes.

event.title: Shadow Brokers leaks begin
event.summary: The Shadow Brokers published tools and exploits allegedly associated with the Equation Group.
event.whyItStillMatters: Leakage of high-end offensive tooling can rapidly convert state-developed capabilities into broad criminal attack risk.

event.title: Mirai / Dyn DDoS attack
event.summary: A massive DDoS attack targeted DNS provider Dyn using the Mirai botnet, disrupting access to major online services.
event.whyItStillMatters: The attack made insecure IoT devices part of the global threat model and highlighted DNS as critical shared infrastructure.

event.title: Cloudbleed
event.summary: Cloudflare disclosed a memory-leak bug that could expose sensitive data from customer websites.
event.whyItStillMatters: Shared cloud and edge infrastructure bugs can create cross-tenant confidentiality risk.

event.title: NYDFS Cybersecurity Regulation
event.summary: New York's cybersecurity regulation took effect for covered financial institutions.
event.whyItStillMatters: The rule helped normalize executive accountability, risk assessment, incident reporting, and program governance in financial services.

event.title: MS17-010 released
event.summary: Microsoft fixed critical SMBv1 vulnerabilities including the flaw later associated with EternalBlue.
event.whyItStillMatters: Organizations had nearly two months to patch before WannaCry weaponized the flaw at global scale.

event.title: EternalBlue exploit released publicly
event.summary: The Shadow Brokers released offensive tooling including EternalBlue.
event.whyItStillMatters: Public release of weaponized exploit code dramatically shortened the path from vulnerability to widespread criminal use.

event.title: WannaCry
event.summary: WannaCry spread globally by exploiting an SMB vulnerability Microsoft had patched two months earlier.
event.whyItStillMatters: It remains a defining example of the cost of delayed patching, unsupported systems, and flat networks.

event.title: NotPetya
event.summary: NotPetya spread from compromised Ukrainian software into organizations around the world and functioned primarily as destructive malware.
event.whyItStillMatters: It remains a textbook example of a targeted supply-chain compromise creating enormous unintended blast radius.

event.title: Equifax breach announced
event.summary: Equifax disclosed a major incident involving highly sensitive consumer identity data.
event.whyItStillMatters: It became a defining case for vulnerability management, data concentration, executive accountability, and identity risk.

event.title: KRACK disclosed
event.summary: Researchers disclosed key reinstallation attacks against WPA2.
event.whyItStillMatters: Even mature, ubiquitous security protocols can fail through subtle state-machine and implementation flaws.

event.title: Uber breach disclosed
event.summary: Uber disclosed a 2016 breach involving personal data for millions of riders and drivers and acknowledged paying the attackers.
event.whyItStillMatters: The incident became a governance case study in breach disclosure, extortion, and executive accountability.

event.title: Meltdown and Spectre
event.summary: Researchers disclosed speculative-execution attacks affecting modern processors.
event.whyItStillMatters: The flaws showed that security failures can exist below the operating system and require coordinated hardware and software fixes.

event.title: GitHub 1.35 Tbps DDoS
event.summary: GitHub experienced a record-setting DDoS attack amplified through exposed memcached servers.
event.whyItStillMatters: Misconfigured Internet infrastructure can be weaponized for enormous amplification attacks.

event.title: Cambridge Analytica scandal breaks widely
event.summary: Reporting revealed large-scale harvesting and political use of Facebook user data through a third-party app ecosystem.
event.whyItStillMatters: The scandal accelerated scrutiny of platform data governance, consent, third-party access, and privacy accountability.

event.title: GDPR becomes applicable
event.summary: The EU General Data Protection Regulation became applicable across member states.
event.whyItStillMatters: GDPR materially changed the global privacy landscape and made data governance, security, and privacy inseparable executive concerns.

event.title: CCPA signed
event.summary: California enacted the Consumer Privacy Act, creating new rights around access, deletion, disclosure, and sale of personal information.
event.whyItStillMatters: CCPA helped establish a U.S. state-level privacy model that influenced subsequent legislation.

event.title: SingHealth breach disclosed
event.summary: Singapore disclosed theft of personal data belonging to about 1.5 million SingHealth patients.
event.whyItStillMatters: Healthcare data has long-term intelligence and identity-abuse value, not merely immediate financial value.

event.title: CISA established
event.summary: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Act formally established CISA.
event.whyItStillMatters: CISA became the central U.S. civilian agency for cyber defense, critical-infrastructure security, and vulnerability coordination.

event.title: Marriott / Starwood breach disclosed
event.summary: Marriott announced unauthorized access to the Starwood reservation database involving a large volume of guest data.
event.whyItStillMatters: The incident highlighted acquisition due diligence, inherited technology risk, data retention, and long attacker dwell time.

event.title: Norsk Hydro ransomware attack
event.summary: Norsk Hydro suffered a ransomware attack that disrupted global operations and forced substantial manual processing.
event.whyItStillMatters: Its response became a widely cited example of transparent crisis communication and resilience.

event.title: Baltimore ransomware attack
event.summary: Baltimore city systems were disrupted by ransomware, affecting email, property transactions, billing, and municipal services.
event.whyItStillMatters: Ransomware can become a public-service continuity problem, not merely an IT outage.

event.title: BlueKeep
event.summary: Microsoft released fixes for a pre-authentication remote-code-execution vulnerability in Remote Desktop Services and warned it was wormable.
event.whyItStillMatters: BlueKeep reinforced the danger of exposed remote administration and end-of-life systems.

event.title: Capital One breach announced
event.summary: Capital One disclosed unauthorized access to personal information associated with credit-card applications and customers.
event.whyItStillMatters: The breach became a cloud-security case study in configuration, identity, metadata services, and least privilege.

event.title: Windows 7 end of support
event.summary: Microsoft ended routine support for Windows 7.
event.whyItStillMatters: End-of-life operating systems become long-term security liabilities when organizations cannot retire or isolate them.

event.title: Twitter account takeover
event.summary: Attackers compromised internal tools and took over numerous high-profile Twitter accounts to promote a cryptocurrency scam.
event.whyItStillMatters: Privileged support workflows can bypass strong user-facing security controls.

event.title: Garmin ransomware outage
event.summary: Garmin experienced a major outage affecting online services, support, and connected-device synchronization following ransomware.
event.whyItStillMatters: Ransomware can disrupt both enterprise operations and customer-facing connected services.

event.title: Düsseldorf hospital ransomware incident
event.summary: A ransomware incident disrupted systems at a German hospital and was associated with diversion of an emergency patient.
event.whyItStillMatters: Cyber incidents in healthcare can create real-world safety consequences.

event.title: FireEye breach disclosed
event.summary: FireEye disclosed that a sophisticated actor stole proprietary Red Team assessment tools.
event.whyItStillMatters: The incident showed the value attackers place on security tooling and the need for rapid public defensive action after compromise.

event.title: SolarWinds Orion compromise
event.summary: CISA warned of active exploitation involving compromised SolarWinds Orion releases delivered through trusted updates.
event.whyItStillMatters: SolarWinds changed how boards and security teams think about software supply chains and privileged management platforms.

event.title: HAFNIUM / Exchange zero-days
event.summary: Microsoft disclosed active exploitation of previously unknown Exchange Server vulnerabilities by a China-based threat actor it called HAFNIUM.
event.whyItStillMatters: Internet-facing messaging infrastructure became a direct path into enterprise networks.

event.title: Colonial Pipeline ransomware
event.summary: Colonial Pipeline experienced a network disruption that led to shutdown of pipeline operations; the FBI later confirmed DarkSide ransomware.
event.whyItStillMatters: A business-system compromise can create physical-world consequences when operations are shut down for safety or containment.

event.title: JBS ransomware attack
event.summary: JBS experienced a ransomware attack that disrupted meat-processing operations in multiple countries.
event.whyItStillMatters: Ransomware against concentrated suppliers can create broader economic and supply-chain risk.

event.title: PrintNightmare
event.summary: Critical Windows Print Spooler vulnerabilities and public exploit code drew widespread attention.
event.whyItStillMatters: Legacy services can create high-impact enterprise attack paths, and disclosure confusion can complicate remediation.

event.title: Kaseya VSA ransomware attack
event.summary: A ransomware campaign exploited Kaseya VSA and affected managed service providers and downstream customers.
event.whyItStillMatters: Management platforms offer attackers enormous leverage because one compromise can cascade into many customers.

event.title: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
event.summary: CISA issued BOD 22-01 and operationalized the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog for federal remediation prioritization.
event.whyItStillMatters: It helped shift vulnerability management toward exploitation evidence and real-world risk rather than severity scores alone.

event.title: Log4Shell
event.summary: Log4Shell exposed remote-code-execution risk in widely deployed Apache Log4j versions through JNDI lookup behavior.
event.whyItStillMatters: It showed how hidden software dependencies can become enterprise-wide security emergencies.

event.title: WhisperGate destructive malware
event.summary: Microsoft described destructive malware targeting Ukrainian organizations and masquerading as ransomware.
event.whyItStillMatters: The campaign foreshadowed use of cyber operations alongside escalating geopolitical conflict.

event.title: HermeticWiper attacks
event.summary: Destructive wiper malware was deployed against Ukrainian organizations immediately before Russia's full-scale invasion.
event.whyItStillMatters: The campaign showed how destructive cyber operations can be integrated into broader military conflict.

event.title: Okta / LAPSUS$ incident disclosed
event.summary: Okta disclosed details around a third-party support engineer compromise after LAPSUS$ published screenshots suggesting access.
event.whyItStillMatters: The incident highlighted identity-provider concentration and privileged third-party support risk.

event.title: Spring4Shell
event.summary: A critical Spring Framework vulnerability could enable unauthenticated remote code execution under affected configurations.
event.whyItStillMatters: It reinforced the challenge of rapidly understanding application-framework exposure across large software estates.

event.title: Costa Rica ransomware crisis
event.summary: Conti ransomware attacks disrupted multiple Costa Rican government agencies and public services.
event.whyItStillMatters: The crisis showed ransomware reaching a level where a national government declared an emergency.

event.title: LastPass development-environment breach
event.summary: LastPass disclosed unauthorized access to portions of its development environment through a compromised developer account.
event.whyItStillMatters: Technical information and developer access can become building blocks for follow-on compromise.

event.title: Uber intrusion
event.summary: Uber disclosed a security incident after an attacker gained broad internal access using social engineering and compromised credentials.
event.whyItStillMatters: The incident reinforced the importance of phishing-resistant authentication and privileged-access segmentation.

event.title: Optus breach
event.summary: Australian telecom provider Optus disclosed a major breach involving customer identity information.
event.whyItStillMatters: Telecommunications providers are high-value targets because they combine identity, account, device, and communications data.

event.title: Medibank cyber incident
event.summary: Australian health insurer Medibank disclosed an incident that later involved theft and publication of highly sensitive customer data.
event.whyItStillMatters: Health and claims data can create extreme privacy harm when stolen and used for extortion.

event.title: OpenSSL CVE-2022-3602 / 3786
event.summary: OpenSSL released fixes for certificate-parsing vulnerabilities that drew broad attention because of the library's ubiquity.
event.whyItStillMatters: The episode reinforced the need for rapid dependency inventory when shared libraries are affected.

event.title: Royal Mail ransomware incident
event.summary: A ransomware incident disrupted Royal Mail's international export services.
event.whyItStillMatters: Ransomware against logistics and postal systems can interrupt physical commerce and supply chains.

event.title: ESXiArgs campaign
event.summary: Widespread ransomware exploitation targeted Internet-exposed VMware ESXi systems.
event.whyItStillMatters: Exposed virtualization infrastructure creates difficult recovery scenarios when hypervisors themselves are encrypted.

event.title: 3CX supply-chain compromise
event.summary: A trojanized 3CX desktop application was used in a supply-chain attack affecting downstream customers.
event.whyItStillMatters: Trusted signed software can become an attack-delivery channel when development or build environments are compromised.

event.title: MOVEit zero-day disclosed
event.summary: Progress Software released patches for a critical MOVEit Transfer vulnerability after signs of active exploitation.
event.whyItStillMatters: One widely used file-transfer product created cascading third-party data exposure across many organizations.

event.title: SEC cybersecurity disclosure rules
event.summary: The SEC adopted rules requiring public companies to disclose material cyber incidents and annual information about risk management and governance.
event.whyItStillMatters: Cybersecurity materiality and governance became explicit securities-law concerns for public companies.

event.title: MGM Resorts cyber incident
event.summary: MGM Resorts disclosed a cybersecurity issue affecting U.S. systems and significant property operations.
event.whyItStillMatters: The event showed how identity compromise and containment can rapidly become visible business-operations problems.

event.title: Caesars Entertainment cyber incident
event.summary: Caesars disclosed a cyber incident involving theft of loyalty-program customer data and payment to attackers.
event.whyItStillMatters: The event reinforced the value of identity data and the role of social engineering in hospitality attacks.

event.title: Citrix Bleed
event.summary: Citrix released updates for a NetScaler vulnerability later associated with session-token theft and session hijacking.
event.whyItStillMatters: Patching alone may not terminate attacker access obtained before remediation; session invalidation can also be required.

event.title: Okta support-system breach
event.summary: Okta disclosed unauthorized access to its customer support case-management system using a stolen credential.
event.whyItStillMatters: Identity providers sit at a uniquely sensitive trust boundary, including supporting systems and uploaded troubleshooting artifacts.

event.title: SEC charges SolarWinds and CISO
event.summary: The SEC filed civil charges against SolarWinds and its CISO alleging fraud and internal-control failures related to cybersecurity disclosures.
event.whyItStillMatters: The case intensified scrutiny of executive cybersecurity statements, disclosure controls, and personal accountability.

event.title: Ivanti Connect Secure zero-days
event.summary: Ivanti disclosed critical vulnerabilities affecting Connect Secure and Policy Secure appliances that were being exploited.
event.whyItStillMatters: Internet-facing security appliances are prime initial-access targets and require rapid patching plus compromise assessment.

event.title: Change Healthcare cyberattack
event.summary: UnitedHealth disclosed a cyberattack affecting Change Healthcare and disrupting claims, payments, pharmacy, and healthcare transactions.
event.whyItStillMatters: Concentration in a critical third-party platform can turn one compromise into a sector-wide operational problem.

event.title: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
event.summary: NIST released CSF 2.0, expanding applicability and adding the Govern function.
event.whyItStillMatters: It formalized cybersecurity as an enterprise governance responsibility, not merely a technical function.

event.title: XZ Utils backdoor
event.summary: A sophisticated backdoor was discovered in XZ Utils 5.6.0 and 5.6.1 after malicious code entered upstream release tarballs.
event.whyItStillMatters: Patient compromise of an open-source project can create risk far beyond the original repository.

event.title: PAN-OS CVE-2024-3400 disclosed
event.summary: Palo Alto Networks disclosed a critical command-injection vulnerability affecting GlobalProtect on certain PAN-OS configurations.
event.whyItStillMatters: Security perimeter devices can become privileged attack paths when Internet-facing components are exploitable.

event.title: Snowflake customer compromises emerge
event.summary: A campaign involving stolen customer credentials affected multiple organizations using Snowflake-hosted data environments.
event.whyItStillMatters: Shared cloud platforms amplify the importance of MFA, credential hygiene, and identity logging.

event.title: Live Nation / Ticketmaster cloud incident
event.summary: Live Nation disclosed unauthorized activity in a third-party cloud database environment containing company data including Ticketmaster information.
event.whyItStillMatters: The incident highlighted third-party cloud concentration and the use of stolen credentials against SaaS and data platforms.

event.title: Polyfill.io compromise
event.summary: Cloudflare reported that the popular polyfill.io JavaScript service could no longer be trusted after malicious code injection.
event.whyItStillMatters: Externally hosted client-side dependencies can silently become supply-chain channels into huge numbers of websites.

event.title: regreSSHion
event.summary: Qualys disclosed an unauthenticated remote-code-execution vulnerability in OpenSSH server on affected glibc-based Linux systems.
event.whyItStillMatters: Fixed vulnerabilities can return through code changes; regression testing matters even for mature infrastructure software.

event.title: CrowdStrike Channel File 291 outage
event.summary: A CrowdStrike content configuration update triggered Windows system crashes at global scale; CrowdStrike said it was not a cyberattack.
event.whyItStillMatters: The outage demonstrated concentration risk in security tooling and the importance of staged deployment, rollback, validation, and resilience.

event.title: EU AI Act enters into force
event.summary: The European Union's AI Act entered into force, establishing a risk-based legal framework for artificial intelligence systems.
event.whyItStillMatters: AI governance became a formal compliance discipline increasingly intersecting with cybersecurity, privacy, and digital trust.

event.title: Salt Typhoon telecom intrusions become public
event.summary: Reports described a China-linked campaign compromising major telecommunications providers and sensitive communications infrastructure.
event.whyItStillMatters: Telecom infrastructure is strategic because compromise can provide access to communications, metadata, and intelligence collection.

event.title: NIS2 transposition deadline
event.summary: EU member states reached the deadline for transposing the NIS2 Directive into national law.
event.whyItStillMatters: NIS2 raised expectations for governance, supply-chain security, incident reporting, and executive accountability.

event.title: EU Cyber Resilience Act enters into force
event.summary: The Cyber Resilience Act entered into force, establishing cybersecurity requirements for products with digital elements.
event.whyItStillMatters: It moves software and hardware security toward lifecycle duty of care, secure-by-design expectations, and manufacturer accountability.

event.title: PowerSchool breach publicly reported
event.summary: PowerSchool disclosed unauthorized access to its student information system environment and data belonging to school districts.
event.whyItStillMatters: Concentrated education platforms hold sensitive data on students, parents, and staff and create broad downstream exposure when compromised.
